title: The Integer Descartes Relation
content: `descartesRelZ` is the parent's curvature relation transplanted from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{Z}$. Restricting the carrier ring to $\mathbb{Z}$ is the whole point of this leaf: it makes "is this curvature an integer?" a first-class question rather than a side condition. Because the relation is a polynomial identity, it is meaningful in *any* commutative ring, and the integer version is what governs integral Apollonian gaskets — packings in which every one of the infinitely many circles has integer curvature.

title: Discriminant Identity: Completing the Square in d
content: The engine of the whole file. Viewing the Descartes relation as a quadratic in $d$, completing the square turns it into the perfect-square statement $(d-(a+b+c))^2 = 4(ab+bc+ca)$. The right-hand side is four times the symmetric product, which plays the role of the discriminant. Both directions of the equivalence collapse to the single polynomial identity `linear_combination -h`, since the two forms differ only by an exact algebraic rearrangement. Writing $S=a+b+c$ and $D=ab+bc+ca$, this is simply $(d-S)^2 = 4D$.

title: The Conjugate Soddy Curvature
content: Given three curvatures $a,b,c$ and one solution $d$, the Descartes quadratic has a second root obtained by Vieta's relation. `soddyReflect a b c d = 2(a+b+c)-d` is exactly that conjugate root. Geometrically it is the curvature of the *other* circle tangent to the same three — the two Soddy circles. Crucially the formula is purely additive: no square roots appear, so the reflected curvature is automatically an integer whenever $a,b,c,d$ are. This integrality of the reflection is precisely why integral gaskets stay integral.
mathContext: $\mathrm{soddyReflect}(a,b,c,d) = 2(a+b+c) - d = d' ,\quad \{d,d'\}\text{ the two roots of the Descartes quadratic.}$

title: Reflection Is an Involution
content: Reflecting the fourth curvature twice returns the original: $\mathrm{soddyReflect}(a,b,c,\mathrm{soddyReflect}(a,b,c,d)) = d$. This is the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ structure of the swap between the two Soddy circles, and it is the local building block of the Apollonian group — the group generated by the four reflections (one per choice of which curvature to swap) that acts on the set of Descartes quadruples and generates the entire gasket. A one-line `ring` identity.

title: Gasket-Generation Step: Integrality Propagates
content: The conjugate of an integer Descartes quadruple is again an integer Descartes quadruple. This is the inductive heart of integral Apollonian gaskets: starting from one integer base quadruple, every circle subsequently inscribed has curvature $2(a+b+c)-d$, an integer combination of integers, and still satisfies the relation. Iterating the four reflections therefore keeps the whole infinite packing integral. The proof is a pure `linear_combination h` — the statement holds in any commutative ring, with no positivity or ordering needed.

title: Vieta Relation (Sum of Roots)
content: The two Soddy curvatures sum to twice the outer-curvature sum: $d + d' = 2(a+b+c)$. This is Vieta's sum-of-roots law for the monic Descartes quadratic $x^2 - 2(a+b+c)x + [(a+b+c)^2-4(ab+bc+ca)] = 0$. It is what makes the reflection $d \mapsto 2(a+b+c)-d$ subtraction-only, hence integrality-preserving.

title: Vieta Relation (Product of Roots)
content: When the relation holds, the two Soddy curvatures multiply to $(a+b+c)^2 - 4(ab+bc+ca)$, the constant term of the Descartes quadratic. Together with the sum relation this fully identifies the monic quadratic whose roots are the two completing curvatures, and exposes the same symmetric product $ab+bc+ca$ that governs the existence dictionary below.

title: Headline: Integrality ⟺ Perfect-Square Discriminant
content: The arithmetic core. Three integers $a,b,c$ can be completed to an integer Descartes quadruple **if and only if** the symmetric product $ab+bc+ca$ is a perfect square. The forward direction is the delicate one: from $(d-(a+b+c))^2 = 4(ab+bc+ca)$ one knows $4 \mid (d-(a+b+c))^2$, but to conclude $2 \mid (d-(a+b+c))$ one needs the *primality of 2* (`Int.prime_two` plus `Prime.dvd_of_dvd_pow`) — divisibility of a square by a prime forces divisibility of the base. Writing $d-(a+b+c)=2m$ then gives $ab+bc+ca=m^2$ after cancelling the factor 4 (`mul_left_cancel₀`). The reverse direction is constructive: take $d=(a+b+c)+2m$ and verify by `linear_combination`.

title: Cast Bridge to the Parent's Real Relation
content: A compatibility lemma: the integer relation `descartesRelZ a b c d` holds iff the parent's real-valued `descartesRel` holds for the casts $(a:\mathbb{R}),\dots$. Because both sides are polynomial equalities and the cast $\mathbb{Z}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is an injective ring homomorphism, `exact_mod_cast` discharges both directions. This is what lets the integer-side reflection theorem be reused to make a statement about *real* curvatures that happen to be integers.

title: Apollonian Integrality (Real Phrasing)
content: The capstone, phrased in the parent's real curvatures. If four real curvatures $k_1,\dots,k_4$ are each integers and satisfy the real Descartes relation, then the reflected Soddy curvature $2(k_1+k_2+k_3)-k_4$ is again (provably) an integer and yields another Descartes quadruple. The proof destructs the integrality witnesses with `obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩`, runs the integer reflection theorem `descartesRelZ_reflect`, and transports back across the cast bridge with `push_cast`/`exact_mod_cast`. This is the precise sense in which 'every circle added to an integral gasket has integer curvature.'
